releases.name: 0.19.4 — Sonar cleanup
releases.body:
# 0.19.4 — Sonar cleanup

Follow-up to 0.19.3. No verifier, trust, or release behaviour change.

## Changed

- `tools.ts`: the durable-storage probe is isolated in `signedRunStorageMarker`, keeping both trust helpers under the cognitive-complexity limit; the manifest failure message uses explicit branches.
- `check-release-consistency.mjs`: explicit `publishConfig` diagnostic branches.
- `publish.yml`: string concatenation in the privileged tag-check here-doc, so GitHub Actions static analysis does not read backticks as command substitution.
- `test-verify.mjs`: `String.raw` for the T56 command fixture.
- Current-version references in the compatibility and packaging docs.

## Upgrade note

0.19.3 is the security release for C-1/M-1/H-1/M-4/C-2 (`GHSA-35g5-xh9r-534x`, affects `<=0.19.2`). 0.19.4 carries the same fixes plus cleanup; either 0.19.3 or 0.19.4 is safe for that advisory.

## Evidence

- `npm test` exit 0; parity 153/153; prompt lint clean; `actionlint -shellcheck=` clean; release consistency 0.19.4 consistent.
- 115 files, zero runtime dependencies.

## Artifact

`heretek-ai-opencode-teamwork-v2-0.19.4.tgz`

`sha256: 64ac098a72a49f918698ac5a6032ced6b74ac05f098776b427a2340583f6ba1e`

releases.name: 0.19.3 — verifier completeness and release-pipeline hardening
releases.body:
# 0.19.3 — verifier completeness and release-pipeline hardening

This release closes the post-0.19.2 verifier and release-pipeline defects. It is a security release; upgrade from 0.19.2 and earlier.

## Security

- **Verifier completeness (C-1):** `verify` refuses `PASS` when `verify/final.json` is missing or `FAIL`, when any planned task report is missing or `FAIL`, when `verify/security-audit.json` is missing or `FAIL`, when the victory audit is missing or `REJECTED`, when the task set is empty, or when the final is unsigned. A PASS now requires a positive final verdict over a non-empty, fully passing evidence set.
- **Rerun output binding (M-1):** the rerun↔report link binds `outputSha256`, not only argv, exit code and byte length.
- **Signed-run legacy downgrade (H-1):** a missing `run.manifest.json` — including a dangling symlink — is refused instead of treated as unsigned legacy when `ctx.storage` records the run nonce/key or any control artifact carries `_auth`. `allowUnsignedLegacy` cannot downgrade a signed run; benchmark mode repeats the refusal at completion.
- **`requireWitness` fail-closed (M-4):** `requireWitness: true` without a configured witness public key fails with `AUTH_WITNESS_UNVERIFIED` instead of accepting a detection-only receipt.
- **Release-pipeline isolation (C-2/H-3):** publishing is tag-only. The OIDC-bearing job runs no repository script, uses a clean npm config and an explicit registry, and rejects repository `.npmrc`/`.yarnrc`/`publishConfig` redirection. `lint` is unfiltered so the required check always reports; CODEOWNERS and an unprivileged dry-run workflow are added.
- **CI attestation (H-2):** marked experimental; it is not claimed as a working OIDC control in 0.19.3.

## Upgrade note

0.19.2 is affected by C-1/H-1 (see `GHSA-35g5-xh9r-534x`, published with this release). Do not rely on a PASS from an affected version when `verify/final.json` is missing or `FAIL`, and do not use `allowUnsignedLegacy` on a signed run.

`verify --rerun` remains arbitrary recorded code. Run it only in a disposable VM/container with no secrets and no shared `.git`.

## Evidence

- `npm test`: 17 tasks, exit 0; 56 verifier tests; release-consistency self-test 34/34.
- Parity: 153/153 (T1 66, T2 65, T3 15, T4 7).
- Runtime: 118 pass, 1 skip (L4), 0 fail against `@opencode/cli@2.4.1`.
- Packed-tarball install: 5 pass; 115 files; zero runtime dependencies.
- `fallow` 0; claim lint 32 files clean; `actionlint -shellcheck=` clean; Rust signer 5/5.

## Artifact

`heretek-ai-opencode-teamwork-v2-0.19.3.tgz`

`sha256: c6d0c5b7f81f695ae9b0343b5b11c30f232604cd0c6e9856c01091787dd39eaa`

Published with npm Trusted Publishing and a Sigstore provenance statement (`logIndex 4117193428`).

releases.name: 0.19.2 — security hardening and release gates
releases.body:
# 0.19.2 — security hardening and release gates

This release closes the verifier trust defects found in the post-0.19.1 audit and makes the release path itself verifiable.

## Security

- **`verify --rerun` trust gate:** no worktree or recorded command is created unless the signed manifest, `verify/rerun.json`, every referenced report, and the rerun link authenticate. `--allow-unsigned` cannot be combined with `--rerun`.
- **`--allow-unsigned`:** accepted only when `run.manifest.json` is absent. A present manifest never downgrades a missing envelope to a warning.
- **Fail-closed trust:** `human-approved`/`ci-attested` without approval enforcement, and `requireWitness` without a usable receipt, are `UNKNOWN`, never PASS. The JSON `trust` object now carries `runTrustLevel`, `approval.status`, and `witness.status`.
- **Fail-closed route evidence (breaking):** on signed runs, `final_verify` refuses PASS for LEMMA (`LEMMA_EVIDENCE_UNSIGNED`), tournament (`TOURNAMENT_EVIDENCE_UNSIGNED`), and document-review (`DOCUMENT_REVIEW_EVIDENCE_UNSIGNED`) until those writers sign evidence. Explicit unsigned legacy runs keep the old behavior. Evidence signing is the next phase; until it lands, those routes on a signed run are blocked at `final_verify`.
- **Attestation input:** no caller-supplied manifest path, no unescaped `GITHUB_ENV` write, and separate test/signing jobs with separate privileges.
- **Publishing:** the OIDC-bearing job is tag-only and publishes the T4-verified tarball after a byte-identical clean re-pack. A branch dispatch can only run the unprivileged dry-run.
- **URL guard:** total deadlines for untrusted fetches, early-refusal socket teardown, retry on per-address timeout, and one OIDC deadline across DNS, discovery, and JWKS.
- **Host drift:** the probe copies the full repository tree and reports install/preflight failures as infrastructure failures, not host drift.

## Release gates

- `l0-parity` (153/153), `pack-t4` (A1/A2/A3 + packed L2 smoke), `release-consistency` (version/tag/CHANGELOG), and process E2E with the real OpenCode 2.4.1 host are distinct CI checks.
- `runtime-l1` installs `@opencode/cli@2.4.1`, runs the process E2E, and asserts **118 pass, 1 skip (L4 live), 0 fail**.
- `npm test` runs 17 L0 tasks, including the release-consistency and attestation-input tests.
- `docs/RELEASE-RUNBOOK.md` records the required checks and tag-only publish boundary.

## Upgrade notes

- **0.18.1 users:** upgrade to 0.19.2. Do not use `verify --rerun` on an untrusted run directory; the recorded commands are arbitrary code even when signed. Use a disposable VM/container with no secrets and no shared `.git`.
- **0.19.1** was merged but never published. 0.19.2 is the first published release containing the 0.19.1 LEMMA doctor-gate and Sonar-residual fixes.
- **Proof/tournament/document-review users:** signed runs are blocked at `final_verify` until evidence signing lands. Use an explicitly unsigned legacy run only if you accept the older trust boundary.

## Verification

- 17 L0 tasks, parity 153/153, runtime 118 pass / 1 skip with real OpenCode 2.4.1.
- T4 5 pass; tarball 115 files, 0 dependencies, no `tests/`, `docs/re/`, or `signer/`.
- `fallow` 0; claim lint 32 files clean; `actionlint` clean; Rust signer 5/5.
- CodeQL: 52 alerts, 0 open, 43 fixed, 9 dismissed.
- SonarCloud `main` @ `52ef2b6`: 1,316 open (7 bugs, 5 vulnerabilities, 1,304 smells); all 12 bugs/vulnerabilities are in the never-shipped `docs/re/` corpus, 0 outside.

releases.name: 0.18.1 — strict tool input validation
releases.body:
Strict tool inputs. OpenCode 2.4.1 does not enforce `additionalProperties:
false`: its input-repair pass deletes undeclared keys before the runtime
validator sees them. Every Teamwork tool now validates its own input, so an
unknown key fails the call with `Tool.Error` and the offending path instead of
being silently dropped.

### Added

- **`strictInput()`** (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tool-schema.mjs`) wraps a JSON
  Schema as a dependency-free Standard Schema. It rejects unknown object
  properties at any depth unless the schema opts in with
  `additionalProperties: true`, and enforces `required`, `type`, `enum`,
  `const`, `anyOf`, `items`, numeric/string/array bounds, and `uniqueItems`.
  Issues carry `{path, message}` and the runtime renders them as
  `Tool.Error("Invalid arguments for tool ...")` with `a.b[0]` paths.
- **Loud schema gate.** Registration asserts every schema uses only the
  validated keyword subset; unsupported constructs (`$ref`, `oneOf`, `not`,
  `format`, `patternProperties` in the source, an unconstrained object, an
  array without `items`) fail loading and `scripts/test-catalog.mjs`.
- **Tests:** `scripts/test-tool-schema.mjs` (top-level and nested unknown keys,
  required, type, enum, array items, bounds, valid input, unsupported
  constructs); L1 A4 now rejects top-level and nested unknown keys through the
  snapshot executor and still accepts a valid call; L2 J1 checks
  `teamwork_plan { bogus: 1 }` and the valid minimal body.

### Changed

- All 26 `teamwork_*` registrations use `input: strictInput({...})`. The
  model-facing JSON Schema is returned unchanged (a non-enumerable empty
  `patternProperties` prevents the host's repair pass from stripping keys and
  is not serialized into the catalog).

### Security

- A caller can no longer rely on the host to discard a mistyped or extra
  argument: the plugin refuses it before `execute`, so nothing is written.
  `additionalProperties: true` records (tournament configuration and a few
  pass-through fields) stay open by design.

releases.name: 0.18.0 — CI attestation
releases.body:
CI attestation, signed by a principal distinct from the run key. A plan can now
require a signed statement from outside the agent's process: the run nonce,
plan hash, prompt hash, report commit and every command's output digest bound
to an Ed25519 key the run does not hold.

### Added

- **`verify/ci/attestation.json`** is an `_auth`-signed artifact over
  `{v, provider, workflow, runId, runAttempt, repository, commitSha, baseSha,
  promptHash, planHash, manifestDigest, commands[], oidc, issuedAt, expiresAt}`.
  Signing uses the existing envelope under a dedicated
  `teamwork-ci-attestation-v1` domain, with `nonce` equal to the signed
  manifest's `runNonce`.
- **Manifest v5** records `attestationPolicy` (`off` | `optional` | `required`,
  default `off`), `attestationKeyId` and `attestationIssuer`. Versions 1–4 read
  as `off`. A re-plan may upgrade `off → optional → required`, never downgrade,
  and cannot change a pinned key id or issuer (`AUTH_STALE`).
- **Enforcement.** `final_verify` fails a `required` run with
  `AUTH_ATTESTATION_MISSING`, `AUTH_ATTESTATION_STALE`,
  `AUTH_ATTESTATION_UNTRUSTED`, `AUTH_ATTESTATION_COMMIT_MISMATCH` or
  `AUTH_ATTESTATION_REPLAY`. A run-key signature is `UNTRUSTED`; a foreign
  run id/nonce is `REPLAY`; a command/output that no report check records is
  `STALE`; `commitSha` must equal every report head. `optional` records the
  status, `off` ignores the artifact. `final.json.evidence.attestation` records
  `{policy, status, code?, commitSha, keyId, issuer}`.
- **`verify`** gains `--attestation-public-key <b64url|@file>`,
  `--attestation-key-id` and `--attestation-issuer`; `--json` now includes
  `attestation: {status, commitSha, keyId, issuer}` and `attested: boolean`.
  Without a key a present attestation is `UNKNOWN` (exit 2), never `PASS`.
- **`scripts/attest-sign.mjs`** is the dev/CI producer (no runtime dependency,
  atomic 0600 write). **`.github/workflows/attest.yml`** is a
  `workflow_dispatch` template gated on the protected default branch, with
  literal test commands and an environment secret; its comments document why a
  dispatch cannot attest arbitrary code.
- **`doctor --security`** reports `attestation_key` (pass for a verify-only
  key, fail for visible private material, warn when `required` has no key).
- **ADR 0018**, `docs/ARTIFACTS.md` schema/policy/codes, `SECURITY.md` residual,
  and L2/L3 coverage plus unit tests for every code, the policy matrix and the
  downgrade refusal.

### Changed

- New plans write manifest version 5. Existing v1–v4 runs keep their meaning and
  `attestationPolicy: "off"`.

### Security

- Establishes: the declared commands ran at the recorded commit, at the recorded
  output digests, under a separate signing identity that bound the signed plan
  and run nonce. Does not establish: the suite is meaningful, a test was not
  edited in the same commit, CI was not compromised, or that the CI key is
  unreachable by the agent's UID. A CI principal reachable by that UID is not a
  boundary.
